edit_summary: Grow dictionary key/value vectors to twice their old size but leave the hash vector at the old capacity.
root_cause: The dictionary stores key, value, and hash arrays as parallel vectors whose capacities must change together during growth.
effect_path: After the parser or public API inserts the 129th entry, dictionary_grow doubles d->size and installs a half-sized hash vector; subsequent inserts, lookups, or unsets use the enlarged d->size while reading or writing d->hash slots beyond the allocation.

guard_p2: After growth, another dictionary_set, dictionary_get, or dictionary_unset operation indexes slots at or beyond the old 128-entry hash capacity.
hardness_reason: The under-allocation is created in a resize helper, while the overflow depends on persistent dictionary occupancy and a later table operation using the new logical capacity.
naturalness_reason: Forgetting one member of a parallel-vector resize is a realistic container maintenance bug.
explanation: The dictionary stores key, value, and hash arrays as parallel vectors whose capacities must change together during growth. After the parser or public API inserts the 129th entry, dictionary_grow doubles d->size and installs a half-sized hash vector; subsequent inserts, lookups, or unsets use the enlarged d->size while reading or writing d->hash slots beyond the allocation.

guard_p2: dictionary_set inserts or replaces the entry, causing xstrdup to scan the unterminated temporary value.
hardness_reason: The missing terminator is introduced in the high-level API truncation path, while the memory read happens later inside the shared dictionary duplication helper.
naturalness_reason: Using sizeof(buffer) as a string payload cap instead of sizeof(buffer)-1 is a plausible API boundary regression.
explanation: iniparser_set copies a bounded value into a temporary string buffer and relies on one reserved byte from the zero-initialized array to terminate the truncated value. A caller sets a value whose length is at least sizeof(tmp_val); memcpy fills the whole stack array, then dictionary_set passes it to xstrdup and strlen reads beyond tmp_val while computing the heap duplicate length.
boundary_invariant: tmp_val must reserve one byte for NUL after copying the truncated public API value.
boundary_case: A value length of ASCIILINESZ+1 fills every byte of tmp_val after the edit.
neighbor_case: A value length of ASCIILINESZ leaves the original zero byte after the copied payload.

root_cause: The parser combines two separately bounded tokens into a single section:key dictionary key, so the temporary buffer must cover both token maxima plus separator and terminator.
effect_path: A valid section name and a valid key that each fit their own ASCIILINESZ buffers reach LINE_VALUE; sprintf then concatenates both into tmp before dictionary_set duplicates the composite key.
guard_p1: The INI file first declares a long section name that fits section[ASCIILINESZ+1].
guard_p2: A later key in that section also fits key[ASCIILINESZ+1], but the combined section:key length exceeds one-token storage.
hardness_reason: The overflow is caused by a cross-field parser invariant: two individually valid tokens become unsafe only when the line classifier and dictionary-key assembly meet in the load loop.
naturalness_reason: Allocating for one normalized token instead of a composite key is a realistic parser integration bug.
explanation: The parser combines two separately bounded tokens into a single section:key dictionary key, so the temporary buffer must cover both token maxima plus separator and terminator. A valid section name and a valid key that each fit their own ASCIILINESZ buffers reach LINE_VALUE; sprintf then concatenates both into tmp before dictionary_set duplicates the composite key.
boundary_invariant: tmp must hold strlen(section) + 1 + strlen(key) + 1 bytes.
boundary_case: A section and key are each near 600 bytes, so each token is accepted but their composite key exceeds ASCIILINESZ+1.
neighbor_case: The same section with a short key, or a short section with the long key, stays within the reduced temporary buffer.
oob_site_expected: src/iniparser.c:884 sprintf writes the combined section:key string past tmp before dictionary_set copies it.

edit_summary: Read continued physical lines using the full line capacity instead of the capacity remaining after the saved continuation prefix.
root_cause: The multiline reader carries a prefix in line[0..last) and must bound the next fgets call by the remaining space after that prefix.
effect_path: A long logical value ending a physical line with a backslash sets last to a nonzero prefix length; the next fgets writes up to ASCIILINESZ bytes starting at line + last and crosses the stack buffer before normal line classification.
guard_p1: The INI file contains a continued value where the first physical line leaves last close to ASCIILINESZ.
guard_p2: The following physical line is longer than the remaining capacity but shorter than ASCIILINESZ, so the relaxed read accepts it into the shifted destination.
hardness_reason: The bad write is gated by parser continuation state from the prior line, not by a single overlong line; ordinary noncontinued long lines still hit the existing line-too-long rejection.
naturalness_reason: Losing the consumed-prefix component in a refill capacity calculation is a plausible streaming parser regression.
explanation: The multiline reader carries a prefix in line[0..last) and must bound the next fgets call by the remaining space after that prefix. A long logical value ending a physical line with a backslash sets last to a nonzero prefix length; the next fgets writes up to ASCIILINESZ bytes starting at line + last and crosses the stack buffer before normal line classification.
boundary_invariant: fgets must receive the capacity remaining after the current multiline prefix stored in line.
boundary_case: A continued logical line has last near 1023 and the next physical fragment contains more bytes than ASCIILINESZ-last.
neighbor_case: A noncontinued line of the same fragment length is rejected by the existing line-too-long check, and a continued fragment shorter than the remaining capacity stays inside line.
oob_site_expected: src/iniparser.c:843 fgets writes past line because the destination starts at line + last but the size argument no longer subtracts last.

guard_p2: Before dictionary_del, the caller performs another lookup, update, or insertion whose hash walk reaches the stale slot.
hardness_reason: The first free and later use cross public dictionary operations and depend on retained table state; a dictionary that is immediately discarded after unset is the nearby non-crashing neighbor.
naturalness_reason: Forgetting to detach a freed slot from an open-addressed table is a realistic lifetime bug.
explanation: Removing a dictionary entry must make the slot unreachable before later lookups scan the table by key and hash. After dictionary_unset frees d->key[i], dictionary_get or dictionary_set on the same dictionary later iterates over the still-non-null slot and calls strcmp on the freed key when the hash matches.
